executiveSummary.line: Strong July revenue and operating profit
One of the year's best margin months
Pipeline remains well ahead of prior year

sections.title: Opening Remarks — Mitchell Kaneff
bullets: Recognized retirees John Sheridan (recently retired) and Wes (departed prior Friday).
Welcomed John Ranson to the team.
Highlighted next-gen leadership, promotions (Izzy and Manny), and growth from within.
Set tone: more transparency, open dialogue, and a "get better, not blame" culture.

sections.title: Financial Performance — July Review
bullets: July 2026 comparative billings: $6.927M prior year.
Positive drivers: volume, favorable customer mix, depreciation savings (~$75K — presses 418/419 fully depreciated), SG&A flat, positive interest variance.
Negative drags: overtime (five-week pay period), factory expenses, freight, repairs & maintenance (+$60K, incl. ~$40K on 418 press die cutter).
Inventory up ~$1M total; finished goods underlying increase only ~$180K — main driver was higher WIP.
Globe outsourcing YTD (7 months): $740K vs $420K same period last year.
Bookings ~$11M+ ahead of last year (~23% higher); billings up ~7%. Revenue counter moved 80 → 85; goal closer to 100% over final five months.
Expecting to produce over $7M this month; billing report ~$6.2–6.3M with two weeks remaining.

sections.title: Manufacturing & Capacity
bullets: Overtime remains elevated due to serialization, glue line demand, window machines, and booming FemCare volume.
Considering additional glue line given heavy outsourcing to Globe — ROI presentation for next meeting.
Mike Sanctuary exploring second soft window machine; quotes being gathered.
Rework takes 12–15 hours per rock job; truck/transport prices up ~$500 average per load.

sections.title: NFL / FemCare Opportunity
bullets: New large FemCare business for the NFL.
First distribution/opening around 9/5–9/13; 50 samples needed at game one; balance due around week three.
Future broken out by team — ~150,000 pieces projected; subsequent quoted up to ~$150,000.

sections.title: Customer Updates
bullets: Revlon / Arden: Two-year contract in negotiation; 20 additional lines to reprice (~800K–1M more cartons); effective January; ~$1.2M payment received.
Oral-B: First order ~15,000 pieces due October; bevel box approved; hologram orientation fix needed.
Sol de Janeiro: Booming; new booking ~$170,000 (butter cream press proof); moving production out of China.
Nest: Billings down ~1.5 but bookings up ~$500K — timing, not concern.
L'Oréal: Down significantly (~$600K holiday promo not repeated).
Estée Lauder: Shortfall not expected to recover in second half.
KDC One / LifePack / Ariana Grande / Chloe: Various programs in progress.

sections.title: Quality Review
bullets: July 2025: 21.26M cartons, 867 deliveries, 202,580 rejected. July 2026: 26.3M+, 899 deliveries, 0 rejected.
External rejects: 3 this year vs goal of 8 (half of last year).
Complaints (6): 2 PNG unglued/bent flaps, bowed cartons, Clinique Christmas transit, Olaplex faded logo, unglued Rock.
Do-overs: 8 jobs, 83,147 cartons (~$22K estimate). Brown Summit downtime: 23% (trending down).
Scorecards 100%: Luxe, Nest, Rock, Revlon, Glossier, Sol de Janeiro, Estée Lauder GQMS. Olaplex 99%; P&G 95%; Scentbird 95%.

sections.title: Global Vision Rollout
bullets: Training complete; verified across QR, Data Matrix, UPC-A barcodes.
Daily file issues tracking: 27 (down ~50% from prior ~50).
Goal: eliminate manual copy check by end of year / early Q1.
Cloud-based AI tool "Verify" in development (live copy vs outline copy).

sections.title: Staffing & HR
bullets: Past month: 5 orientations, 15 no-shows; ~5 glue line interviews scheduled this week.
Talent from Vuoyant closing: operator/maintenance mechanic, quality person starting Sept 1, 2 packers.
Succession: Big Manny replacing Gordy (through year-end); Little Manny → day-shift supervisor; Andrew Price possible third-shift supervisor return.
Housing challenge: local rent ~$1,500/month; building costs up ~50%.
Ryan Scott third-operator proposal: ~9 hrs/day × 250 days × 6,000/hr = 13M+ sheets/year potential; trial on day shift first.

sections.title: Technology & AI — Steve Habermas
bullets: Copilot: ~50 licenses; training program being finalized. Voice AI agent capturing institutional knowledge.
Traba / Neo platform: POC for scheduling, purchasing/estimating, reporting — Scott Tanzer's data team.
ERP: 3 consultants shortlisted; outside firm to document processes (~20% manager time, ~2 months from September).
AMS/WMS: ESL inventory report, schedule change reason codes, quote automation, barcode scanning.
Roanoke bandwidth upgrade scheduled August 24; warehouse Wi-Fi upgrade underway.
Boston Dynamics "Spot" demo requested week of October 10 — target $250K–$275K financed.

actions.action: Full ROI presentation on new glue line machine (cost, utilization, capacity analysis).
Gather quotes for additional software window machine; categorize Globe spend by gluing vs die-cutting.
Fix video conferencing audio, mic, speaker, and camera tracking before next meeting.
Complete Roanoke bandwidth upgrade (Aug 24) and warehouse Wi-Fi; roll out Neo/Traba training within ~2 weeks.
Update pre-press SOPs to include Global Vision.
Prepare top 3 Global Vision customer benefits for Thursday sales meeting.
Develop day-shift third-operator trial plan with overtime-savings numbers.
Continue recruiting for glue line and third-shift supervisor role.
Finalize Revlon/Arden two-year contract; execute NFL first shipment (25K) and monitor 150K follow-on.
Track Oral-B (Oct), Sol de Janeiro, FemCare, and KDC One growth.
Coordinate Boston Dynamics Spot demo (week of Oct 10) with ROI business case.
Evaluate smaller Epson printer options for customer offices (Sol de Janeiro sticky-customer strategy).
